We've covered multiple stories about Apple Vision Pro applications in medical settings. This week, Stryker announced the completion of the first surgery using an innovative app on Vision Pro.

The procedure was a hip arthroscopy, utilizing the SportSuite Vision app, which brings "critical digital content into the surgeon's virtual space." Content includes arthroscopy imaging, HipCheck, HipMap, and CT scan images.

Below is Stryker's introduction of the app:

SportSuite Vision brings critical digital content into the surgeon's visual space, allowing them to view physical objects in the operating room while simultaneously using digital tools such as arthroscopy imaging, HipCheck, HipMap, and CT scan images. During arthroscopic surgery, surgeons often rely on multiple displays positioned in various locations throughout the operating room to access imaging and surgical data. By integrating multiple data sources into the surgeon's field of view, this technology can reduce reliance on traditional displays and support a more streamlined, ergonomic surgical workflow.

SportSuite Vision received FDA De Novo authorization on July 17. Stryker states that this app is the first FDA-authorized app for intraoperative use with Vision Pro.

Additionally, this week Pfizer also announced that it is using Apple Vision Pro to "create an unforgettable immersive experience" to "showcase" its commitment to "conquering cancer."
